newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression forms in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression forms in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: The 10th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season formed in the Gulf of Mexico Friday, threatening to become a tropical storm on Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 11 p.m. EDT (0300 GMT), Tropical Depression number 10 was 200 miles (320 km) south-southeast of Brownsville, Texas, at latitude 23.0 north and longitude 96.3 west. The storm's location also put it about 65 miles (110 km) east-northeast of Tampico, Mexico.
The storm was nearly stationary on Friday evening and little movement was expected during the next 24 hours.

Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (55 kph) and forecasters said strengthening was possible. "The depression could strengthen to become a tropical storm on Saturday," the National Hurricane Center said.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
The depression would be named Josephine if it strengthened into a tropical storm.
